title: the DSG lands of Deepearth opener

banner.title: THE DSG LANDS OF DEEPEARTH OPENER, R533: printed p. 75 (pdf 76) - the Deepearth setting frame and the connecting-passage generation: the frame (the lands presented in detail as a campaign setting, the party gaining many levels without exploring the entirety; the alternative example-of-the-ecosystem view, use-and-discard, expandable, the realms occupying no more area than a moderately small nation; the numbered-area rough detail with the mapping-in-more-detail requirement; the page-114 three-dimensional and geomorphic mapping referrals; and the hollow-earth-below note with the shafts from the lowest level), the connecting passages (all passable to human-sized characters, the vertical obstacles and water currents handled per area or generated randomly), the water passages (the rivers with their map-readable flow directions, the indicated waterfalls with map-scale drops, the rest navigable by boat with a skilled pilot and a little luck; the 1d6-x-10 width generation for the 10-60-foot spread, the width constant for one mile, the drift reroll - 2-5 the same, 1 shrinking 10 feet or 5 at the 10-foot floor, 6 growing 10 feet even beyond 60; the 1d6 temperature - 1-5 very cold, the 6 heat check with the second d6 - 1 cool-slightly-warmer, 6 boiling hot, 2-5 proportional; only the boiling water unsafe for unprotected characters), the tunnels (the human-passable diameters, mostly natural caverns, the 10-percent-per-10-miles carved chance, the carved uniform 10-foot diameter and height with no sudden obstacles; the 33-percent-per-mile obstacle chance with the 10d10 cliffs, the 20d10-deep 4d10-wide chasms, the cave-in remnants and the water-quicksand-oil-tar pools, never closing the passage; the 3d20 cavern widths from 3 to 60 feet, constant for 1d20-x-100 feet of 100-2,000, the 1/3 change chance with the 3d20 reroll; and the unintelligent dwellers - scavengers, fungi, molds and lichens - the intelligent denizens only passing through, the banished renegade bands the exception), and the area details (the framework-not-full-detail rule, the 300-foot-square as 30-by-30 graph squares, and the DMG page-169 Random Dungeon Generation referral)
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~9584-9712) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 176 = the printed p. 75 window); the compiled-tables appendix has no reprint of these procedures. A CLEAN-READ ROUND with one settled garble: the djvu cavern-width formula reads "(3420)" and the Capture layer reads "(3d20)" - settled as 3d20 by the Capture read, corroborated by the 3-60-foot range (the standing die-notation OCR class); every other load-bearing number agrees in both reads - the 1d6-x-10 widths, the drift bands, the temperature bands, the 10% carved chance, the 33% obstacle chance, the 10d10/20d10/4d10 obstacle dice, and the 1d20-x-100 constancy. The map pages (printed pp. 76-77) are graphics and pin nothing this round. SEAMS: the DMG Random Dungeon Generation (page 169), the R518 water travel (the navigable-by-boat rule), the R531 geography (the cavern-width generation), and the R503 re-grain. A ZERO-FLIP ROUND: the pp. 75-98 Deepearth child remains open until the setting lands in full (the R527 precedent - the gap report is NOT in the git add). Nothing auto-credits.
banner.sentinel: A procedural round: the numbers pin as consts per the R508 convention - the waterway width generation (1d6 x 10, the 10-60 spread, the drift bands with the 5-foot floor), the temperature bands (1-5 cold, the 6 heat, the second d6 with the boiling 6), the tunnel carving (10%, the uniform 10 feet), the obstacles (33% per mile, the 10d10 cliffs, the 20d10-deep 4d10-wide chasms), the cavern widths (3d20, the 3-60 range, the 1d20-x-100 constancy, the 1/3 change chance), and the area-details example (the 300-foot square, the 30 squares, the DMG page 169). The frame and dwelling prose pin as bools. The DMG/R518/R531 seams are noted; the Deepearth child stays open; nothing auto-credits.

prev_record: - R532 LANDED 2026-10-17: commit 3c3fc98 (census 455 -> 456,
pushed f52a044..3c3fc98), THE DSG CULTURES OF THE
UNDERDARK, printed pp. 73-74 (pdf 74-75), the third
DM-section child - the values and objectives frame (the
races relying less on trade and interaction than the
surface races, the environment forcibly segregating
them; trade governed more often by proximity than by
alignment - an evil race more likely to trade with a
nearby neutral race than a distant evil one; and the
monster-encyclopedia referral), and the eight race
write-ups: the drow (the strongly matriarchal society
with females holding all power in government, military
and home; the Lolth worship with the 6th-level-and-
higher testing and the drider failures; the spider-like
scorpions, pedipalp and solifugud; the web-pattern
buildings with the traps channeling prey to the
center; the aged-only cannibalism under population
pressure; the treaty-breaking making alliances
reluctant; and the long-term objective of ruling all
subterranean races and controlling underworld access),
the kuo-toa (the race past its prime struggling to
retain its holdings, its inability to cooperate making
it susceptible to conquest; the Sea Mother worship as
the one unifying element with the holy-war dream; the
5% insanity breeding the monitor class; and the
slave-acquiring brute force, treachery or barter), the
duergar (the disciplined and orderly evil allowing
dominance; the mountain-and-hill-dwarf kinship in
mining and metal-and-stone work; the fiendish
imprisoning traps with slow painful deaths; the slave
labor with complete disregard for welfare; the
mercilessness and torture love; the extermination over
driving off to eliminate reprisal; and the
sculpture-and-metalworking craft trade for slaves and
devices), the mind flayers (the aboleth the only
non-hostile race with the sinister-connection legends;
the brain hunger leaving bodies to the scavengers; the
racial quest to douse the fires of the sun itself; the
probability-travel escape from difficult odds; the
rigidly psionic-ranked society with slave labor and
slave food; the life-form experiments with their
hostile hybrids; and the immunity-bought-with-slaves
trade and the temporary aboleth pacts), the aboleth
(the most alien culture from the human point of view,
coldly ruthless with torture serving no rational
purpose; the intended complete control of the
underworld beginning with the underground waters - the
main reason for the kuo-toan waning; the obscene mind
flayer pacts with the illithid as a temporary tool; the
godless reverence of the greater aboleth, one to six
per city at four times the size and Hit Dice, the
repositories of the alien knowledge; and the remote
casually-guarded slave cities), the derro (the small
savage bands never in large communities, raiding near
the surface; the chaos and intraracial violence; the
stealing over working and the short-lived duergar and
drow pacts; and the 20-year savant war cycle ending in
utter defeat but recovered by the high reproductive
rate), and the cloakers (the true children of the
earth with the Elemental Plane of Earth ties; the most
intelligent of their type over the lurkers, miners,
trappers and mantari servants; the violence answering
all contact attempts; the toolless structureless
culture with its instinctive community sense; and the
guerrilla warfare and kin-sacrificing defense). A
CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every
number (djvu ~lines 9268-9460, Capture idx 172-174;

consts.name: dndlWaterWidthDice
consts.comment: the waterway width roll: 1d6 multiplied by 10.

consts.name: dndlWaterWidthSides
consts.comment: the waterway width die is a d6.

consts.name: dndlWaterWidthMultFt
consts.comment: the 1d6 result is multiplied by 10 feet.

consts.name: dndlWaterWidthMinFt
consts.comment: the narrowest waterway section is 10 feet wide.

consts.name: dndlWaterWidthMaxFt
consts.comment: the widest standard waterway section is 60 feet.

consts.name: dndlWidthSameLow
consts.comment: the width-drift roll: on a 2-5 the river remains at approximately the same width for the next mile.

consts.name: dndlWidthSameHigh
consts.comment: the upper bound of the same-width drift band.

consts.name: dndlWidthShrinkFt
consts.comment: a drift roll of 1 decreases the river width by 10 feet.

consts.name: dndlWidthFloorFt
consts.comment: a river already only 10 feet wide decreases by 5 feet instead of 10 on a shrink roll.

consts.name: dndlWidthGrowFt
consts.comment: a drift roll of 6 expands the river width by 10 feet - even if this makes it wider than 60 feet.

consts.name: dndlWaterColdHigh
consts.comment: the temperature roll: on a 1-5 the river is very cold.

consts.name: dndlWaterHeatRoll
consts.comment: on a 6 some heat is reaching the water, and a second d6 determines how warm.

consts.name: dndlWaterWarmLow
consts.comment: the second roll: on a 1 the water is cool, but slightly warmer than normal.

consts.name: dndlWaterBoilRoll
consts.comment: on a 6 the water is boiling hot - the only temperature unsafe for unprotected characters to swim or fall into.

consts.name: dndlCarvedChancePct
consts.comment: about 1 out of every 10 miles of connecting tunnel has been carved by intelligent creatures.

consts.name: dndlCarvedDiaFt
consts.comment: an excavated tunnel is a uniform 10-foot diameter and height, with no sudden obstacles such as cliffs or chasms.

consts.name: dndlObstaclePct
consts.comment: a base 33% chance per mile that an obstacle lies in the path of the PCs exploring natural caverns.

consts.name: dndlCliffDice
consts.comment: the obstacle cliff height roll is 10d10 feet.

consts.name: dndlCliffSides
consts.comment: the cliff height die is a d10, ten of them.

consts.name: dndlChasmDepthDice
consts.comment: the obstacle chasm depth roll is 20d10 feet.

consts.name: dndlChasmDepthSides
consts.comment: the chasm depth die is a d10, twenty of them.

consts.name: dndlChasmWidthDice
consts.comment: the chasm width roll is 4d10 feet.

consts.name: dndlChasmWidthSides
consts.comment: the chasm width die is a d10, four of them.

consts.name: dndlCavernDice
consts.comment: the connecting-cavern width roll is 3d20 feet.

consts.name: dndlCavernSides
consts.comment: the cavern width die is a d20, three of them (the djvu 3420 garble settled by the Capture read).

consts.name: dndlCavernMinFt
consts.comment: the narrowest connecting cavern is 3 feet wide.

consts.name: dndlCavernMaxFt
consts.comment: the widest connecting cavern is 60 feet.

consts.name: dndlConstDice
consts.comment: a cavern width remains constant for 1d20 x 100 feet.

consts.name: dndlConstSides
consts.comment: the constancy distance die is a d20.

consts.name: dndlConstMultFt
consts.comment: the constancy die is multiplied by 100 feet.

consts.name: dndlConstMinFt
consts.comment: the shortest constancy run is 100 feet.

consts.name: dndlConstMaxFt
consts.comment: the longest constancy run is 2,000 feet.

consts.name: dndlChangeChancePct
consts.comment: after the constancy run the cavern stands a 1/3 chance of changing width - reroll the 3d20 if indicated.

consts.name: dndlSquareFt
consts.comment: the area-details example: a dungeon described as occupying a 300-foot-square area.

consts.name: dndlSquaresPerSide
consts.comment: the 300-foot square means a 30-by-30 square section of graph paper, not one huge room.

consts.name: dndlDmgPage
consts.comment: the Random Dungeon Generation system referral: DMG page 169.

bools.name: dndlSettingForCampaign
bools.comment: the lands of Deepearth are presented in detail as a setting for the underground campaign: the known varieties of intelligent life each claim a portion, and a party can gain many levels and overcome towering obstacles without exploring Deepearth in its entirety.

bools.name: dndlExampleToAdapt
bools.comment: alternatively regard the lands as an example of the underground ecosystem - utilize the aspects you like, disregard others, expand as you wish; as presented the realms occupy no more area than a moderately small nation, with potential for many such realms under the lands and seas.

bools.name: dndlAreaKeyRoughDetail
bools.comment: each numbered map area is presented in rough detail - the overall geography, the major inhabitants and resources, and any unique features - and each area must be mapped in more detail to run a campaign there.

bools.name: dndlThreeDimReferral
bools.comment: for three-dimensional mapping detail see page 114; geomorphic mapping is described there too and can be a great time-saver for PCs spending much time in the regions of Deepearth.

bools.name: dndlHollowBelowNote
bools.comment: if employing one of the hollow earth theories, the hollow-earth region lies below the areas depicted on the Deepearth map - create shafts or tunnels leading down from the lowest level.

bools.name: dndlPassagesHumanSized
bools.comment: all connecting passages are large enough to be passable to human-sized characters; other factors such as vertical obstacles or water currents are handled in the area description or generated randomly by the DM.

bools.name: dndlRiversFlowMap
bools.comment: the map waterways are rivers flowing through the dark reaches; the flow direction is easy to determine from the map, the rivers proceeding at a rapid pace or slower, sometimes almost stagnant.

bools.name: dndlWaterfallsIndicated
bools.comment: all vertical drops are indicated on the map - use the map scale to determine how far a waterfall drops; all other waterway sections are navigable by boat, assuming a skilled pilot and a little luck.

bools.name: dndlWidthMileConst
bools.comment: a waterway width remains constant, with minor fluctuations, for one mile, after which the drift d6 is rolled again.

bools.name: dndlWaterBoilOnlyDanger
bools.comment: the water in underground rivers is usually numbingly cold; only water that is boiling hot is unsafe for unprotected characters to swim or fall into, the 2-5 results meaning a degree of warmth proportional to the roll.

bools.name: dndlTunnelsHumanPass
bools.comment: the tunnels connecting the larger realms are all of sufficient diameter to allow a human to pass, and often much wider; in most cases they are natural caverns.

bools.name: dndlObstacleExamples
bools.comment: the obstacles: a cliff of 10d10 feet height, a chasm 20d10 feet deep and 4d10 feet wide, the remnants of a cave-in, or a large pool of water, quicksand, oil, or tar - the obstacle never completely closes off the passage.

bools.name: dndlUnintelligentDwellers
bools.comment: unintelligent monsters including scavengers occasionally live in the passages, as do fungi, molds and lichens - but intelligent creatures do not dwell here; encountered drow and other denizens are passing through, though renegade bands banished from their homelands might eke out an existence in the tunnels.

bools.name: dndlFrameworkNotFullDetail
bools.comment: the map shows much too large an area to be fully detailed in the volume - an overall framework is given and the DM is free to fill in the necessary details.

bools.name: dndlSquareMeansGraph
bools.comment: general information indicates the overall parameters: a 300-foot-square dungeon maps as a 30-square by 30-square graph section, not as one huge room 300 feet on a side.

bools.name: dndlDmgRandomDungeon
bools.comment: if there is no time to prepare a map, use the Random Dungeon Generation system in the DMG, page 169.
